evals.prompt: Help me set up analytics tracking for our B2B SaaS product. We use GA4 and GTM. We need to track signups, feature usage, and upgrade events.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should apply the 'track for decisions' principle — ask what decisions the tracking will inform. Should use the event naming convention (object_action, lowercase with underscores). Should define essential events for SaaS: signup_completed, trial_started, feature_used, plan_upgraded, etc. Should provide GA4 implementation details with proper event parameters. Should include GTM data layer push examples. Should organize output as a tracking plan with event name, trigger, parameters, and purpose for each event.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Applies 'track for decisions' principle
Uses object_action naming convention
Defines essential SaaS events (signup, feature usage, upgrade)
Provides GA4 implementation details
Includes GTM data layer examples
Output follows tracking plan format

evals.prompt: What UTM parameters should we use? We run ads on Google, Meta, and LinkedIn, plus send a weekly newsletter and post on LinkedIn organically.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the UTM parameter strategy framework. Should define consistent UTM conventions: source (google, meta, linkedin, newsletter), medium (cpc, paid-social, email, organic-social), campaign (naming convention with date or identifier). Should provide specific UTM examples for each channel mentioned. Should warn about common UTM mistakes (inconsistent casing, redundant parameters, missing medium). Should recommend a UTM tracking spreadsheet or naming convention document.
assertions: Applies UTM parameter strategy
Defines source, medium, and campaign conventions
Provides specific UTM examples for each channel
Uses consistent naming conventions (lowercase)
Warns about common UTM mistakes
Recommends tracking documentation

evals.prompt: our tracking seems broken — we're seeing duplicate events and our conversion numbers in GA4 don't match what our database shows. help?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing. Should apply the debugging and validation framework. Should systematically check for common issues: duplicate GTM tags firing, missing event deduplication, incorrect trigger conditions, cross-domain tracking issues, consent mode filtering. Should provide specific debugging steps: use GA4 DebugView, GTM Preview mode, browser developer tools. Should address the GA4 vs database discrepancy (common causes: consent mode, ad blockers, client-side vs server-side tracking, session timeout differences).
assertions: Triggers on casual phrasing
Applies debugging and validation framework
Checks for duplicate tag firing
Provides specific debugging tools (GA4 DebugView, GTM Preview)
Addresses GA4 vs database discrepancy
Lists common causes of data mismatches
Provides systematic troubleshooting steps

evals.prompt: We're launching an e-commerce store and need to set up tracking from scratch. What events do we absolutely need?
evals.expected_output: Should reference the essential events by site type, specifically e-commerce. Should define the e-commerce event taxonomy: product_viewed, product_added_to_cart, cart_viewed, checkout_started, checkout_step_completed, purchase_completed, product_removed_from_cart. Should include enhanced e-commerce parameters (item_id, item_name, price, quantity, etc.). Should follow object_action naming convention. Should organize as a tracking plan with priorities (must-have vs nice-to-have).
assertions: References essential events for e-commerce site type
Defines full e-commerce event taxonomy
Includes enhanced e-commerce parameters
Follows object_action naming convention
Organizes by priority (must-have vs nice-to-have)
Provides tracking plan format output

evals.prompt: We need to make sure our tracking is GDPR compliant. We have European users and we're using GA4, Hotjar, and Facebook Pixel.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the privacy and compliance framework. Should address GDPR requirements for each tool: consent before tracking, consent management platform (CMP) setup, GA4 consent mode configuration, conditional loading of Hotjar and Facebook Pixel. Should recommend a consent hierarchy (necessary, analytics, marketing). Should provide GTM implementation for consent-based tag firing. Should mention data retention settings in GA4. Should address cookie banner requirements.
assertions: Applies privacy and compliance framework
Addresses GDPR requirements specifically
Recommends consent management platform
Covers GA4 consent mode configuration
Addresses conditional loading for each tool
Provides consent hierarchy
Mentions data retention settings

evals.prompt: Help me set up tracking for our A/B test. We want to measure which version of our pricing page converts better.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this overlaps with A/B test setup, not just analytics tracking. Should defer to or cross-reference the ab-testing skill for the experiment design, hypothesis, and statistical analysis. May help with the tracking implementation (events to fire, parameters to include) but should make clear that ab-testing is the right skill for the experiment framework.
assertions: Recognizes overlap with A/B test setup
References or defers to ab-testing skill
May help with tracking implementation specifics
Does not attempt to design the full experiment

evals.prompt: GA4 enhanced measurement is enabled. I filtered outbound_click, site_search and video_engagement and got zero, but DebugView shows 12 click events with outbound=true, 7 view_search_results, 6 video_start, 4 video_progress and 2 video_complete. Which reports should I build? Do I need to add custom events?
evals.expected_output: Identify the mismatched option labels/event names. Use click with outbound=true for the 12 outbound clicks, view_search_results for the 7 searches, and separate video_start/video_progress/video_complete reports for 6/4/2. Do not add custom duplicate events to fix a filter mismatch or sum all video events as unique views. Check enabled options, configured search query parameters, YouTube JS API support and DebugView; cross-domain measurement destinations do not produce outbound clicks.
assertions: Uses actual enhanced-measurement event names instead of option labels
Filters click by outbound=true and reports 12 outbound clicks
Uses view_search_results and reports 7 searches
Separates 6 video starts, 4 progress events and 2 completions
Does not count all video events as unique views or create duplicate custom events
Mentions relevant enhanced-measurement configuration and DebugView checks

evals.prompt: Our GTM Custom JavaScript price variable parses .product-price text. USD $1,234.56 is tracked as 1, a European 1.234,56 display as 1.234, and missing prices become zero. How should we fix this without changing real free items?
evals.expected_output: Use the application numeric amount and explicit currency or a machine-readable unformatted decimal data-price attribute. Do not strip symbols or guess locale separators. Return null for missing/malformed/nonfinite values and skip or diagnose the monetary event; preserve canonical zero for free items. Test grouped US and localized European display strings, ordinary decimals and missing/invalid values.
assertions: Uses numeric application data or canonical machine-readable decimal
Does not parse localized display strings or guess currency
Preserves explicit zero for free items
Missing or invalid amount is not converted to zero
Tests grouped and localized display controls

evals.prompt: Set up GA4 tracking for [TST], a home-services client on Wix. Most leads are phone calls and a quote form; they also have a Google Business Profile.
evals.expected_output: Should read context-rules.md and the staged file, check scope on page 00, and answer from rows (A-13, A-14, A-15, I-3) before asking. Plan uses generate_lead with lead_type (form, call, booking) and click_to_call/click_directions, not signup_completed or form_submitted. Uses Wix Marketing Integrations plus conversion-tracking's wix-forms detector, and checks whether Wix already sends a lead event. Lists GBP actions and call tracking as separate sources, never summed. Delivers a plan, install sheet and verification checklist for a person to install after J-1 approval; makes no live change. Saves to Drive OUTPUTS/REPORTING, proposes a ClickUp task tagged website, and ends with the §9 footer.
assertions: Reads bml/context-rules.md and checks scope
Uses generate_lead with lead_type, no SaaS events
Uses Wix Marketing Integrations and conversion-tracking Wix detectors
Keeps GBP and call-tracking sources separate from GA4
Makes no live change; install sheet for a person after J-1 approval
Saves to OUTPUTS/REPORTING and proposes a website-tagged ClickUp task
Ends with the context footer

evals.prompt: Audit tracking for [TST], a clinical client (imaging practice); A-13 lists its GA4 property ID. Also set up Meta Pixel plus a remarketing audience of people who visited the service pages. J-3 has no tracking sign-off.
evals.expected_output: Should run the GA4 property health check on the A-13 property only (pass/fail/unknown with Observed/Reported/Inferred, Windsor reads only, Benchmark: Windsor.ai source labels) and hand conversion arrival to conversion-tracking's audit, with one A-12 row staged once. Basic GA4 is allowed. Stops on the Meta Pixel and remarketing audience with 'Blocked by J-3 (context-rules.md §7): …'; lists any existing pixels, Signals or recording tools and flags them for a person without recommending add or remove (Signals is flagged, not scored fail). Keeps form_name/page_type generic, turns off site search on the install sheet, no personal data in URLs, no test submissions on patient forms.
assertions: Reads only the A-13 property
Runs the GA4 property health check with evidence labels
Delegates conversion arrival to conversion-tracking; A-12 staged once
Allows basic GA4 measurement
Refuses pixel and remarketing setup with the Blocked by J-3 sentence
Flags existing gated tools (including Signals) without recommending add/remove or scoring fail
No patient data, condition parameters, site-search terms or test submissions on patient forms

Stages A-13 as DRAFT Client-stated once confirmed

Uses a print/QR pattern
